item.title: Mainland welcomes growing discussion in Taiwan on "one country, two systems": spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
Mainland welcomes growing discussion in Taiwan on "one country, two systems": spokesperson BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese mainland welcomed growing discussion in Taiwan about national reunification and a proposed "one country, two systems" framework for the island, a spokesperson said Wednesday. Chen Binhua, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, was responding to a question about a Taiwan scholar who had published three consecutive articles on social media discussing the proposed framework. "It is normal to have different opinions and debates between people on the mainland and Taiwan in the process," Chen said. "We believe more of our compatriots in Taiwan will break free from the ideological constraints and 'information cocoons' created by the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities, and increasingly recognize the advantages of the 'one country, two systems' and the inclusiveness of the Taiwan solution it offers," he said. The Taiwan question is left by a full-blown civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the remnants of the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, and the People's Republic of China (PRC) was founded under the leadership of the CPC. The unresolved civil war and foreign interference have left the two sides of the Taiwan Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation, though the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. Peaceful reunification under "one country, two systems" is the best approach to achieving national reunification, Chen said. "The specific form of implementation of 'one country, two systems' in Taiwan will fully take into consideration the realities in Taiwan, fully absorb the opinions and suggestions of people from all sectors on both sides of the Strait, and fully safeguard the interests and sentiments of Taiwan compatriots," he said. While discussions about reunification grow in Taiwan society, the DPP authorities continue to challenge the one-China principle. Taiwan leader Lai Ching-te has recently again argued that United Nations General Assembly Resolution 2758 was not related to Taiwan. Chen said such attempts would only bring humiliation upon Lai and the DPP authorities and were bound to fail. No matter what they do, Chen said, they cannot alter the legal and factual reality that Taiwan is part of China, undermine the international community's adherence to the one-China principle, or halt the historical trend toward national reunification. The U.N. General Assembly adopted Resolution 2758 in 1971 by an overwhelming majority, clarifying that the PRC government is the sole legal government representing the whole of China. This resolution, from the perspective of international law, completely eliminated possibilities of "two Chinas" or "Taiwan independence."

item.title: DPP slammed for move to curb cross-Strait ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
DPP slammed for move to curb cross-Strait ties A Chinese mainland spokesman denounced the Democratic Progressive Party authorities in Taiwan on Wednesday for using various measures to obstruct cross-Strait exchanges, stressing that national reunification remains an inevitable historical trend. Chen Binhua, a spokesman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks at a regular news conference in response to the DPP authorities' recent measures targeting cross-Strait exchanges. Local tourism authorities in Taiwan have asked travel agencies to collect the personal information of tourists traveling to the mainland, raising privacy concerns on the island. Chen denounced the move as "a despicable tactic" by the DPP authorities to threaten and intimidate Taiwan people from visiting the mainland and to interfere with cross-Strait personnel exchanges. "The aspiration of people on both sides of the Taiwan Strait to draw closer together, along with the momentum of cross-Strait exchanges and cooperation, is unstoppable," Chen said. Meanwhile, DPP supporters have recently shown heightened sensitivity to expressions associated with the mainland and simplified Chinese characters. In one case, a man was accused of being a mainland spy after he was seen watching a video containing simplified Chinese characters at a train station. A subsequent police investigation found that he was simply watching a financial management course. "From treating Taiwan people's use of mainland expressions as a major threat to viewing the use of certain simplified Chinese characters as evidence of espionage infiltration, the DPP authorities are becoming increasingly paranoid," Chen said. He added that the DPP's anti-mainland approach has undermined mutual trust across the Taiwan Strait and would further fuel a climate of "green terror" in Taiwan society. Despite the DPP authorities' obstruction, cross-Strait economic ties have continued to grow. Trade between Taiwan and the mainland reached $221.8 billion from January to July, up 26.5 percent year-on-year, Chen said. Mainland exports to Taiwan totaled $62.17 billion, up 31.6 percent, while imports from Taiwan to the mainland reached $159.63 billion, up 24.7 percent. Chen also addressed recent discussions among Taiwan people about the implementation of the "one country, two systems" principle in Taiwan. Li Ci-ze, an associate professor at Changhua University of Education in Taiwan, recently published a series of articles on social media discussing the implementation of "one country, two systems" in Taiwan, which have triggered heated debate across the Strait. "We are pleased to see more and more Taiwan compatriots recognize the inevitability of reunification and begin to understand and discuss the specific implementation of 'one country, two systems' under Taiwan's circumstances," Chen said. He stressed that peaceful reunification and "one country, two systems" are the best way to realize national reunification. He said the implementation of this solution in Taiwan would take the island's actual situation and the interests of the Taiwan people into full account, while also incorporating suggestions from various sectors across the Taiwan Strait. "National reunification is an unstoppable historical trend. For our compatriots in Taiwan, it is not an optional question, it is one which must be answered," he said.

item.title: Taiwan has never been a country and will never be one: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
Taiwan has never been a country and will never be one: spokesperson BEIJING, Sept. 8 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Tuesday that Taiwan has never been a country and will never be a country, adding that the Lai Ching-te authorities' deliberate distortion of UNGA Resolution 2758 once again revealed their separatist nature for "Taiwan independence." Mao made the remarks at a regular news briefing when asked to comment on Lai's claim that China is contorting UNGA Resolution 2758 and that Taiwan is a "sovereign independent nation." Lai Ching-te authorities' rhetoric will not change the historical and legal fact that the two sides of the Taiwan Strait belong to one and the same China, nor will it undermine the international community's steadfast commitment to one China, she said. UNGA Resolution 2758 solemnly reaffirmed the one-China principle, which "decides to restore all its rights to the People's Republic of China and to recognize the representatives of its Government as the only legitimate representatives of China to the United Nations," she said. From political, legal and procedural aspects, the resolution resolved once and for all the question of the representation of the whole of China, including Taiwan, in the UN, she said, adding that it made clear that there is only one seat of China in the United Nations, and there is no such thing as "two Chinas" or "one China, one Taiwan."

item.title: DPP attempts to rewrite colonial history
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
DPP attempts to rewrite colonial history Editor's note:The Taiwan question is a key focus for China and the international community. China Daily is publishing a series of reports to track hot Taiwan-related topics and address disinformation from the Democratic Progressive Party administration. SONG CHEN/CHINA DAILY A fragmentary narrative of history under Japanese colonial rule has been used by Taiwan authorities to reshape the historical memory and identity of people on the island in an effort to serve their separatist agenda, analysts said. As Imperial Japan's first overseas colony, Taiwan endured significant suffering under Japanese colonial rule from 1895 to 1945. Hundreds of thousands of people in Taiwan were killed by the Japanese colonial authorities, while more than 2,000 women on the island were forced into sexual slavery as "comfort women". The 50-year colonial rule ended 81 years ago when Japan was defeated in World War II. However, the Democratic Progressive Party authorities have sought to erase the history of Japanese aggression in Taiwan while glorifying Japanese colonial rule in an attempt to sever the island's historical and cultural ties with the Chinese mainland, as reflected in their statements about the period and efforts to revise history textbooks. On Aug 15, the anniversary of Japan's surrender in World War II, the Chinese mainland strongly condemned visits by Japanese officials to the Yasukuni Shrine. The shrine honors Class-A Japanese war criminals from World War II and is regarded as a spiritual symbol of Japanese militarism. In contrast, the DPP authorities in Taiwan said they "respected diverse perspectives on historical events in Japan". The Lai Ching-te authorities' stance on this historical period has remained ambiguous, with the authorities largely avoiding discussion of Taiwan's resistance against Japanese aggression. This approach has drawn criticism from both Taiwan and the Chinese mainland. Analysts said Lai's "colonial nostalgia" is intertwined with his pursuit of "Taiwan independence" by relying on Japan. They also warned that reshaping the collective memory of Taiwan society for political purposes could endanger regional peace and stability, particularly amid efforts by Japan's right wing to remilitarize the country. Resistance against imperial rule Taiwan was ceded to Japan under the Treaty of Shimonoseki after the Qing Dynasty (1644-1911) was defeated in the First Sino-Japanese War in 1895. From armed resistance and guerrilla warfare to nonviolent movements to defend the island, the people of Taiwan never ceased their resistance to Japanese colonial rule, with more than 600,000 people sacrificing their lives in the struggle. Wang Xiaoping, a research fellow at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' Institute of Modern History, said Taiwan's resistance to Japanese invasion is traced back to the Mudan Incident, when indigenous groups fought against Japanese forces in 1874. "The anti-Japanese struggles of Taiwan people were part of modern China's resistance to foreign aggression," Wang said. "Unfortunately, this history is neither duly respected nor fully represented in today's Taiwan society." In March, Lai claimed at a public event that Japan's colonization of Taiwan was aimed at promoting the so-called Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere. The remark was condemned on both sides of the Taiwan Strait as a "desecration of the martyrs" and a "betrayal of the nation". In fact, Japan's efforts to develop and build up the island served the empire's goals of colonial economic exploitation and oppression, as well as its subsequent strategy of southward expansion into Southeast Asia, Wang said. "Agricultural Taiwan, Industrial Japan "was the guiding principle of Japanese colonial policy, under which Taiwan was transformed into a supplier of raw materials and a market for Japanese manufactured goods. The Japanese colonial authorities reaped most of the profits generated on the island, while resources such as rice, sugar, timber and minerals were shipped to Japan, Wang said. Meanwhile, throughout the Japanese colonial period, the Japanese governor-general maintained autocratic rule through the police apparatus. The people of Taiwan were deprived of the right to vote or stand for election and were subjected to strict and often brutal police control. Following the outbreak of Japan's full-scale war of aggression against China in 1937, Japanese colonists further launched the "Kominka Movement", an aggressive campaign of Japanese cultural assimilation in Taiwan. Local people were forced to learn Japanese and change their names to Japanese names. Chinese-language newspapers were banned, and traditional Chinese folk practices were abolished. "It sought to remold Taiwan's people into so-called imperial subjects loyal to the Japanese Emperor, aiming to erode their Chinese national identity," Wang said. "The ultimate goal was to serve Imperial Japan's war efforts." However, people in Taiwan preserved Chinese culture in various ways, and it remained vibrant on the island, he added. Although the movement failed, the ideological imprint of Japanization persisted among some individuals even after Taiwan's return to China in 1945. These remnants later contributed to the rise of "Taiwan independence" separatism, negatively affecting relations with the mainland, according to studies on Taiwan's history. Today, separatist forces on the island have distorted and selectively portrayed history to glorify the modernization achieved under Japanese imperial rule, while deliberately overlooking the suffering and sacrifices of the people of Taiwan, Wang said. "This incomplete historical narrative diminishes the sacrifice of anti-Japanese resistance martyrs and obscures the significance of Taiwan's return to China," Wang said. He added that it misleads younger generations into believing that "colonization brought modernization", a view directly at odds with global anti-colonial trends. Erasing history On Aug 15 last year, marking the 80th anniversary of Japan's surrender in World War II, Lai published an article framed around the concept of the "end of war", thereby evading explicit reference to Japan's surrender or the Chinese victory. Furthermore, while Taiwan authorities consistently opposed visits by Japanese officials to the Yasukuni Shrine between 2000 and 2015, they have maintained complete silence on the issue for a decade following the DPP's ascension to power in 2016. Hung Hsiu-chu, former chairwoman of the Chinese Kuomintang, wrote on the same day that "the territorial losses, devastation and humiliation inflicted by colonial imperialism are a history that people on both sides of the Taiwan Strait must never forget". While attempting to downplay Taiwan's resistance to Japanese colonization, Lai has amplified the "legacy" of Japanese rule. He paid tribute on bended knee to Yoichi Hatta, a Japanese colonial-era engineer, arguing that Taiwan should "remember the source of its water" when considering Japan. Wang pointed out that the DPP's passive stance on atrocities committed by the Japanese militarists during World War II stems from "Taiwan independence" separatism, which is rooted in the legacy of the Japanese "Kominka Movement" on the island. "The DPP also curries favor with Japan to advance its separatist agenda, hoping to leverage external forces to contain the mainland," Wang said. "They are reshaping the identity of Taiwan people and altering young people's historical perception to weaken their Chinese identity." Chi Sing, publisher of The Observer magazine based in Taiwan, said that the authorities under Lai and Tsai Ing-wen have never expressed a clear stance on the issue over the past decade, while repeatedly stressing that "Taiwan and Japan have close relations and jointly maintain regional peace". This, Chi said, fully reveals their ambition to rely on external forces to seek "independence". Despite the DPP's attempts to rewrite history, civil groups and individuals in Taiwan have been striving to preserve shared memories of resistance to external aggression. In August, protests were organized on the island to oppose Japan's right-wing military expansion and interference in the Taiwan question. Because people on both sides of the Taiwan Strait share a common Chinese identity, the DPP's "colonial nostalgia" strains cross-Strait relations by widening the psychological divide, Wang warned. He added that this biased historical narrative risks fracturing Taiwan society, lowering vigilance against Japanese right-wing forces and undermining regional stability. Recently, the Japanese government has adopted a series of measures to expand its defense forces and weapons. Chi said that Japan's remilitarization would certainly "not be a blessing for the people of Taiwan", as it would jeopardize peace in the Asia-Pacific region and even globally. KMT's Hung emphasized that history has repeatedly demonstrated that when China is divided, external parties gain, warning that Taiwan should avoid becoming a pawn for foreign forces seeking to exploit the region.

item.title: Taiwan's reunification with motherland inevitable, mainland spokesman says
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
Taiwan's reunification with motherland inevitable, mainland spokesman says A Chinese mainland spokesman said on Wednesday that reunification with the motherland is inevitable for Taiwan, not a matter of choice, noting that peaceful reunification under "one country, two systems" is the best way to achieve national reunification. Chen Binhua, spokesman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, stated that national reunification is an unstoppable historical trend. "For Taiwan compatriots, reunification is not an optional question, but a mandatory one," he said at a regular news conference. Recently, Li Ci-ze, an associate professor from Changhua University of Education in Taiwan, published three articles on social media discussing the implementation of "one country, two systems" in Taiwan. The articles sparked heated discussion among readers on both sides of the Taiwan Strait, with some describing it as "a rare breakthrough text". In response, Chen said at the Wednesday news conference that peaceful reunification and "one country, two systems" are the best way to achieve national reunification. He stressed that the framework's specific implementation in Taiwan would fully take into account the island's actual situation and incorporate suggestions from various sectors on both sides of the Taiwan Strait. The interests and sentiments of the people in Taiwan would also be fully taken into consideration, he said. Chen said more and more Taiwan compatriots are recognizing the inevitability of national reunification and beginning to understand and discuss the specific implementation of "one country, two systems" under Taiwan's circumstances. Meanwhile, they are offering suggestions and ideas for the plan through various channels. "We are pleased to see this," Chen said, adding that differences of opinion and debates are normal in the process. "We believe that more Taiwan compatriots will break through the ideological constraints and information barriers imposed by the Democratic Progressive Party authorities and come to recognize the advantages of 'one country, two systems' and the inclusiveness of the Taiwan plan," Chen said.

item.title: Surge in passenger traffic highlights close cross-Strait bonds on 'mini three links' routes
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
Surge in passenger traffic highlights close cross-Strait bonds on 'mini three links' routes Passenger traffic on the "mini three links" routes between Taiwan and the mainland surged during the summer vacation, highlighting the close bonds across the Taiwan Strait, a mainland spokeswoman said Wednesday. Zhang Han, spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, noted that the strong performance of these routes reflects the deep connections between people on both sides of the Strait. The ferry routes, connecting coastal areas in Fujian province with the islands of Jinmen and Matsu, are crucial for travel and exchanges between the mainland and Taiwan. During the summer, the Xiamen-Jinmen route alone operated 1,550 ferries, accommodating 386,400 passenger trips — an increase of 11.4 percent and 24.1 percent year-on-year, respectively. On Aug 23, daily passenger trips on this route exceeded 7,900, the highest since operations resumed in 2023. To manage the increased traffic, mainland authorities enhanced service capacity by extending operating hours, streamlining customs procedures, strengthening maritime safety, and improving passenger services. Smart systems were also implemented to ensure efficient and smooth clearance. Zhang emphasized that the "mini three links" routes have been operating safely and efficiently, and she encouraged more people from Taiwan to travel to the mainland using these routes.

item.title: Mainland condemns Taiwan's increased 'defense' budget
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
Mainland condemns Taiwan's increased 'defense' budget A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Wednesday condemned the Taiwan authorities led by Lai Ching-te for escalating cross-Strait tensions by increasing the island's "defense" budget, reaffirming the mainland's unwavering resolve to combat "Taiwan independence" separatist activities. Zhang Han, a spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks at a regular news conference, saying that Lai's authorities have stubbornly adhered to a separatist stance while disregarding the mainstream public aspiration for exchanges, cooperation, development and peace in Taiwan. Recently, the Democratic Progressive Party authorities proposed raising Taiwan's annual "defense" budget to more than NT$1 trillion ($31.4 billion) in 2027, surpassing that threshold for the first time. Lai claimed the move aims to ensure that "defense" resources are transformed into "reliable defensive capabilities". Zhang accused the authorities of escalating cross-Strait confrontation and squandering public resources in a futile attempt to "resist reunification by force" and pursue "Taiwan independence" through force. "They are utterly overestimating their capabilities and will only bring severe disaster to the people of Taiwan," she said. Zhang reiterated that the mainland's resolve and ability to safeguard national sovereignty and territorial integrity are unwavering and strong, leaving no room for any form of "Taiwan independence" separatist activities. "We hope that Taiwan compatriots recognize the harm and danger of 'Taiwan independence' separatism, firmly oppose such separatist actions, and steadfastly uphold the common homeland of the Chinese nation as well as their own safety and well-being," Zhang added.

item.title: Mainland denounces Taiwan authorities' move to increase defense spending
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
Mainland denounces Taiwan authorities' move to increase defense spending BEIJING -- A Chinese mainland spokeswoman on Wednesday criticized the decision of Taiwan authorities led by Lai Ching-te to raise the island's defense budget in 2027, saying it would only bring grave disaster to the people in Taiwan. Zhang Han, spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks in response to a question about the island's defense budget of more than NT$1 trillion (about $31 billion) for 2027, which Taiwan authorities led by Lai Ching-te said was aimed at strengthening its defense capabilities and demonstrating its resolve to defend itself. Zhang said Taiwan authorities led by Lai Ching-te have stubbornly adhered to their separatist stance of seeking "Taiwan independence," disregarding the mainstream public opinion on the island that calls for "peace, development, cross-Strait exchanges and cooperation." They have instead stoked confrontation across the Taiwan Strait and squandered public funds in pursuit of their independence agenda, Zhang said, adding that such efforts are "simply beyond their capabilities" and will only have serious consequences for the people of Taiwan. "We are unwavering in our resolve and formidable in our ability to safeguard national sovereignty and territorial integrity, and will never leave any room for separatist activities seeking 'Taiwan independence' in any form," Zhang noted. She called on people in Taiwan to recognize the dangers of "Taiwan independence" separatism, firmly oppose such activities, and safeguard the common home of the Chinese nation. Taiwan's executive authorities approved the island's 2027 general budget on Aug 20, with defense spending rising sharply to over NT$1 trillion for the first time. The defense budget accounts for roughly 29 percent of total government expenditure, meaning that about 29 out of every 100 New Taiwan dollars in government spending would go toward defense.

item.title: Taiwan Affairs Office of Xingyang Organizes Compatriots and Families of Taiwan Origin to Experience Intangible Cultural Heritage
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-04
Taiwan Affairs Office of Xingyang Organizes Compatriots and Families of Taiwan Origin to Experience Intangible Cultural Heritage Source: Taiwan.cnUpdated: 2026-09-04
Sep 4(Taiwan.cn)—On August 27, the Taiwan Affairs Office of Xingyang organized representatives of Taiwan compatriots and their family members residing locally to take part in an immersive observation？and？experience activity featuring intangible cultural heritage. During the event, participants visited distinctive cultural sites including the Chang？style Boxing Training Institute, the Yellow River Chengni Inkstone Art Museum, and the Hou？dian Village Hollow？out Cultural and Creative Park to learn about the preservation and inheritance of local intangible cultural heritage resources. With on？site briefings, craft demonstrations and interactive hands？on sessions, Taiwan compatriots and their families gained detailed insights into the historical evolution, inheritance lineage, technical features and inheritance system of each intangible cultural heritage item. Rooted in Xingyang’s local intangible cultural heritage resources, the activity allowed Taiwan compatriots and their families to get close？up exposure to the profound heritage and humanistic spirit of traditional martial arts, craftsmanship and folk arts. It further deepened their understanding of the historical bonds that bind people across the Taiwan Strait as one origin with shared culture and ethnicity. (Jointly reported by Taiwan.cn and the Taiwan Affairs Office of Xingyang) Related Stories

item.title: Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for obstructing cross-Strait exchanges
item.description:
Published: 2026-02-11
Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for obstructing cross-Strait exchanges BEIJING, Feb. 11 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson has condemned Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities for imposing restrictions and obstacles on cross-Strait exchanges in pursuit of their "Taiwan independence" agenda and selfish gains. The DPP authorities, led by Lai Ching-te, are the biggest obstacle to cross-Strait interactions and their acts have drawn strong criticism from various sectors in Taiwan, Zhu Fenglian, a spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said at a regular press briefing on Wednesday. Zhu expressed the hope that Taiwan compatriots will firmly oppose the retrogressive actions of the DPP authorities and promote exchanges and cooperation across the Taiwan Strait in various fields. She noted that cross-Strait flight routes have been disrupted due to interference from the DPP authorities, with previously operated destinations yet to resume normal operations. In 2025, the average passenger load factor on cross-Strait routes reached 80 percent, reflecting the strong need for direct flights between the two sides of the Strait, Zhu said. "We hope that the Taiwan side will heed public opinion and lift unreasonable restrictions on cross-Strait air transport as soon as possible," she added.
